_about: What the firing line's picture needs beyond the courses and the physics: the eye's height, the clock hour of each time of day, the colours of each season measured from photographs taken at the two ranges in 2016 and 2017 (docs/LOOK.md; a phone camera took them, so each is within about 15 percent of the truth), the haze, and the sizes of the things on the range. Colours are hex strings; every figure is an estimate with its basis. The picture never changes a shot.

eyeHeightFt.estimate: the eye of a shooter seated at a bench, about 4 ft above the shelter's concrete floor (a 30-inch bench top and the head about 18 in above it)

morning.estimate: the clock hour the morning's light is computed for, Pacific standard time (daylight saving ignored): soon after the range opens, the same basis as the weather's tempAt for the morning

midday.estimate: half past twelve, Pacific standard time, the middle of the day's shooting

afternoon.estimate: half past three, Pacific standard time, the late-afternoon light of the September and October photographs (15:00 to 16:10 by their file names)

monthDay.estimate: the sun is computed for the middle day of the day's month

greenByMonth._about: How green the ground cover is in each month, 1 the February-to-April green, 0 the June-to-November straw: from the photographs' dates (vivid green on 12 February and 25 March 2017; straw and tan on 11 September 2016; dry gold on 21 October 2017; drying by 8 April 2017 at the rifle line) and the winter rains that green these hills from December.

1.estimate: January: greening after the first rains

2.estimate: February: the vivid green of the 12 February photographs

3.estimate: March: still vivid green on 25 March

4.estimate: April: green at the canyon, already drying on the rifle line's slopes by 8 April

9.estimate: September: straw and tan, the 11 September photographs

10.estimate: October: dry gold, the 21 October photographs

11.estimate: November: dry, the first rain some years

palette._about: Measured colours, medians of small patches of the photographs, by range and season (docs/LOOK.md). The canyon course's figures stand for the rifle line too where it has none of its own.

sky.estimate: winter sky, 12 February 2017 at 12:58 (the March photographs give #4391d9)

sunlitSlope.estimate: sunlit grass slope, February and March 2017

scrub.estimate: scrub, or a shaded green slope

floor.estimate: the dirt floor, February (to #afa190 in March)

scrub.estimate: the dark olive of the scrub in late summer; not measured, the green scrub's figure darkened and warmed

shadedSlope.estimate: a dry slope in shade; not measured, the sunlit dry slope at the ratio the green pair shows

floor.estimate: the dirt floor, paler and dustier, September

sunlitHills.estimate: sunlit dry hills at last light

shadowHills.estimate: hills in shadow at last light

paintRedInSun.estimate: red paint in strong sun, seen through the spotting scope: the red washes toward pink

paintRed.estimate: the plates' red paint as painted and faded by the sun; not measured, a red that the sun and the glass wash to the measured pink (#af787b)

strikeMark.estimate: the pale grey-white where bullets have chipped the paint

boardWhite.estimate: the white boards, which strong sun bleaches to pure white through the scope

boardNumberBlue.estimate: the blue stencilled numbers at the boards' feet

moundDirt.estimate: the fresh brown dirt mound each plate stands in front of

floor.estimate: turned dirt in low sun, October

turbidityClear.estimate: the sky model's turbidity on a dry day (Preetham's scale: 2 is very clear, 10 is hazy)

turbidityHumid.estimate: the turbidity on the most humid day the weather draws (humidity near 0.9): a pale, milky sky

visibilityDryMi.estimate: the distance at which things fade into the haze on a dry, hard-lit day (a Santa Ana day): the far hills stay sharp

visibilityHumidMi.estimate: the same on the most humid day: the 1,000-yard plate pales and the ridge beyond goes soft

rayleigh.estimate: the sky model's Rayleigh scattering (three's Sky default is 2): a little more, so the sky away from the sun is the saturated blue the February and September photographs show

mieClear.estimate: the sky model's Mie (haze) scattering on a dry day: low, a clear sky

mieHumid.estimate: the same on the most humid day: a bright ring around the sun and a pale horizon

sunIntensity.estimate: the sun's strength in the scene (three's units, where a Lambert surface reflects its albedo divided by pi), chosen so a sunlit slope at midday matches the measured colours within the tolerance docs/LOOK.md gives

skyIntensity.estimate: the sky's fill light from above, the same basis

groundBounce.estimate: light bounced up from the pale floor, the same basis

exposure.estimate: the picture's exposure (the tone curve's scale, ACES filmic, applied in the last pass to the scene drawn in linear light), chosen so a sunlit slope at midday and the dirt floor match the measured colours within the tolerance docs/LOOK.md gives (range-day-six; was 0.85 when the scene was drawn clipped into an 8-bit texture with no tone curve)

skyScale.estimate: the sky model's brightness against the ground's: the model's own units, scaled so the sky high up matches the measured blue

skyTintShare.estimate: how far the sky's hue is pulled from the physical model's toward the season's measured sky colour (0 the model alone, 1 the measured hue with the model's light): the model, lit by a white sun, draws a paler, greyer blue at 18 degrees up than the photographs show

rimShare.estimate: the soft warm rim at the edge of the scope's picture is a few percent of the radius wide: six percent

rimColor.estimate: the rim's brown-orange, from the spotting-scope photographs

softness.estimate: how much softer than the naked eye the picture is toward the edge of the glass, 0 none to 1 strong; the middle is left sharp (range-day-six: a good scope shows more, not less)

contrast.estimate: the picture's colour contrast through glass against the naked eye's 1 (range-day-six: nearly all kept)

bleach.estimate: how far strong highlights wash toward white through glass (the boards bleach to pure white)

wash.estimate: how far strong colours wash toward the light through glass: the red paint measured through the spotting scope in strong sun is a washed pink (#af787b)

fringe.estimate: a touch of colour fringe (lateral chromatic aberration) toward the edge of the scope's picture, 0 none to 1 strong

startF.estimate: the temperature above which heat shimmer begins to show through magnification

fullF.estimate: the temperature at which it is strongest

amplitudeMoa.estimate: the distortion at its strongest at 1,000 yards, in minutes of angle: about a plate's width wobble at that distance through a high-power scope

boardWidthIn.estimate: the white target boards in their rows are about 2 ft wide

boardHeightIn.estimate: and about 3 ft tall, standing on a short frame

boardGapIn.estimate: the gap between boards in a row

boardsPerRow.estimate: about thirty boards side by side in each row (numbers 01 to 30 at the first line)

boardRowsYards.estimate: the first target line, numbers 01 to 30: a board's number appears to begin with its hundreds of yards
the third row, numbers in the 400s

nearGroupBoards.estimate: two groups of four boards (01 to 04 at the left, 05 to 08 at the right) stand nearer, on low mounds

notchDepthFt.estimate: the first target line is a notch cut into a low terrace about a man's height deep

moundWidthFt.estimate: the mound of fresh dirt behind each plate, about 8 ft across

shelterWidthFt.estimate: the open-sided shelter is long: 60 ft of it is drawn

shelterDepthFt.estimate: about 14 ft deep, bench to drip line

shelterRoofFt.estimate: the corrugated roof about 9 ft above the concrete floor

benchAheadFt.estimate: the bench top begins about 1.5 ft ahead of the eye

benchHeightFt.estimate: a bench top about 31 in high

brushCountFull.estimate: how many bushes the Full picture stands on the slopes, placed where the photograph is dark with scrub

brushFarYards.estimate: bushes are stood out to about 1,500 yards; beyond that the photograph alone carries the scrub

treeHeightFt.estimate: the lone trees on the ridge and the cluster by the wash, about 25 ft

depth._about: How finely the picture tells a surface from another behind it. The scene asks for a 24-bit depth buffer (DEPTH_COMPONENT24 in src/scene/post.mjs, on Full and on Light), the finest WebGL2 guarantees and the coarsest the scene may get since it asks for no other; the camera's near and far planes spread those steps over the distance. At a distance z (metres) one step is z² × (1/near − 1/far) / (2^24 − 1). A surface less than a step behind another at the same place on screen shows through it in broken, shifting dots (depth fighting): Dan saw them on the white boards at 200 yards through the scope on his phone, 19 Nov 2026, where the boards' posts stood half a centimetre behind the sheets. Every post stands at least stepsApart steps behind what it holds, worked out at the farthest it stands.

cameraNearM.estimate: the camera's near plane, half a metre: the bench top begins 1.5 ft ahead of the eye and is the nearest thing drawn

cameraFarM.estimate: the far plane, 20 km: the hills beyond the far square and the sky dome

bits.estimate: the depth buffer's bits: the scene asks for DEPTH_COMPONENT24 (src/scene/post.mjs), which WebGL2 guarantees; a coarser one is never given

stepsApart.estimate: two steps so that the two surfaces can never round to the same depth whichever way each rounds, and two more for the depth interpolated across a pixel's samples and a frame's wobble

boardPostStandOffM.estimate: the nearest face of a board's post stands this far behind the board's sheet: 4 steps at the farthest board row, 400 yards (365.76 m), where a step is 365.76² × (1/0.5 − 1/20000) / (2^24 − 1) = 0.01595 m; 4 × 0.01595 = 0.0638, rounded up to 0.065 (before range-day-seven: 0.005)

platePostStandOffM.estimate: the nearest face of a plate's post stands this far behind the plate's back: 4 steps at the farthest plate, 1,000 yards (914.4 m), where a step is 914.4² × (1/0.5 − 1/20000) / (2^24 − 1) = 0.0997 m; 4 × 0.0997 = 0.399, rounded up to 0.4 (before range-day-seven the post's face sat inside the plate's thickness, 0.14 cm behind its front face)

nearSpacingM.estimate: the ground mesh's spacing at the firing line, the survey's own 1 m

growth.estimate: each row of the mesh is this much farther apart than the one before, so the mesh is finest along the first hundreds of yards

halfAngleDeg.estimate: the mesh fans 70 degrees either side of the line of fire: everything a hold-off or a look around can bring into the view

columnsFull.estimate: columns across the fan in the Full picture, finer near the line of fire

rowsFull.estimate: rows out to the far square's edge in the Full picture

detailTileM.estimate: the close-up surface detail made in code repeats every 3 m: clods, crumbs and dry stems

detailFadeYards.estimate: the detail fades out by 300 yards, where the photograph's own pixels are finer than the view

measureS.estimate: the first visit draws the Full picture for two seconds and counts the frames

minFps.estimate: fewer frames a second than this over those two seconds picks the Light picture for the device

ground._about: The ground's surface (range-day-six; its surfaces photographed since range-day-eight): how the picture sorts each pixel into dirt, grass, scrub, rock and scree, how each class's photographed material is laid, and the small relief. Every figure is an estimate with its basis or a reading of the material's library.

floor.estimate: the small relief of the packed dirt floor, as a share of its scan's own measured slopes: 1, the scan's relief as measured (range-day-eight; it was 0.6 of the code-made clods)

grass.estimate: the small relief under grass and scrub, as a share of the scans' measured slopes: 1, as measured (range-day-eight; it was 0.5 of the code-made clumps)

rock.estimate: the small relief of bare rock and scree, as a share of the scans' measured slopes: 1, as measured (range-day-eight; it was 1.3 of the code-made stones)

steepDeg.estimate: a face steeper than about 45 degrees holds no soil and reads as bare rock or scree; the canyon's grassy walls stand at 30 to 40 degrees, its headwall and the cut banks steeper

hollowM.estimate: a cell 2 m below the mean of its neighbours 4 m away counts as fully in a crease: the picture darkens creases and gullies up to this depth

hollowDarkening.estimate: how much the sky's light is cut in a full crease, 0 none to 1 black

clearanceM.estimate: the sun-and-shade picture records how far the sun's ray clears the ground, clamped at 4 m either way, so the edge between sun and shade falls where the clearance crosses zero

sheenRock.estimate: the slight sheen of bare rock and stones toward the sun, 0 none

lanesM.estimate: tire tracks on the floor run on lanes about 3.5 m either side of the line of fire

gaugeM.estimate: the two ruts of a lane are a pickup's track width apart, about 1.6 m

darkening.estimate: a rut is about 14 percent darker than the floor beside it

reachYd.estimate: the tracks fade out by the first boards, about 90 yards out

photoFinestPx.estimate: the photograph is never shown finer than 3 of its own pixels (about 2 m): magnified past that its compression shows as blocks; the survey's relief and the detail carry the finer structure. The ground's sorting into dirt, grass, scrub and rock reads it twice as coarse again

materials._about: Each class's photographed material (data/terrain.json, surfaces): how much ground one copy of its picture covers.

source.note: the scan's ground size, 4000 mm across, as Poly Haven's listing gives it (dimensions) for dry_ground_rocks; the listing as the Ground workflow fetched it is on the scratch branch range-day-eight-fetch, ground-fetch/raw/

the scan's ground size, 2000 mm across, as Poly Haven's listing gives it (dimensions) for withered_grass; the listing as the Ground workflow fetched it is on the scratch branch range-day-eight-fetch, ground-fetch/raw/
ambientCG's listing gives Grass001 dimensionX 140 and dimensionY 140 with no unit; read as centimetres, a 1.4 m patch (as Ground106's 250 is read as 2.5 m)
ambientCG's listing gives Ground106 dimensionX 250 and dimensionY 250 with no unit; read as centimetres, a 2.5 m patch, the size of the library's other photographed ground patches

the scan's ground size, 2700 mm across, as Poly Haven's listing gives it (dimensions) for rock_face_03; the listing as the Ground workflow fetched it is on the scratch branch range-day-eight-fetch, ground-fetch/raw/

the scan's ground size, 3000 mm across, as Poly Haven's listing gives it (dimensions) for gravel_ground_01; the listing as the Ground workflow fetched it is on the scratch branch range-day-eight-fetch, ground-fetch/raw/

materialAlbedo.estimate: how much of a material's own brightness and colour pattern shows over the palette's colour, 0 none to 1 as photographed: as photographed, since a lower figure measured as less detail than the code-made ground it replaced (range-day-eight, verify 6)

hexTiles.estimate: the triangles each material is shifted by are about half a copy of its picture across (2 m on the 4 m dirt): smaller than one copy, so no two neighbouring copies can match, and large enough that each copy still shows whole clods and tufts

hexSharpness.estimate: how sharply each point leans to its triangle's nearest corner (a power on the three blend weights, as Mikkelsen's hex-tiling paper does): at 6 most of the ground shows one copy unblended, so the material keeps its contrast; the seams lean to the higher picture

macroScale.estimate: each material is laid a second time at five times its size (7 to 20 m across): the clumps and patches a hillside shows through a scope at 600 yards, which a scan of a few metres does not hold, and detail farther out where the fine copy has faded

macroShare.estimate: how strongly that second, larger copy shows over the fine one, 0 none to 1 as photographed: a little under 1, so the magnified pattern reads as patches and not as giant blades

macroShareLight.estimate: on Light the larger copy shows as photographed: Light's 512-pixel pictures are softer and its fine copy is drawn only close in, so the larger copy carries the hillside's detail through the scope

lightFineFade.estimate: on Light (512-pixel pictures) the fine copy of a material is drawn only where a screen pixel covers less than a 128th of it, fading out by a 32nd (on Full a 32nd to an 8th): farther, its blades and crumbs are below a pixel and the larger copy carries the ground, for half the picture reads
the same, the far end of the fade

heightBlend.estimate: how far a material's own height (0 to 1) pushes its class's weight where two classes meet: at 0.35 the higher picture wins over about a third of the blend, so dirt shows between tufts and stones stand out of grit instead of a soft smear

varyM.estimate: the slow variation that decides where rock is bare and grass thin repeats over about 120 m (the code-made detail's coarse tile times five, as before range-day-eight), now made from a smooth noise instead of a picture

reliefShadowM.estimate: a material's relief throws a shadow about 2 cm long with the sun 45 degrees up (to three times that as the sun drops): the 'clods and crumbs with hard small shadows' of the spotting-scope photographs

reliefShadowDepth.estimate: the height difference, as a share of the material's whole relief, that makes a full shadow

reliefShadowDark.estimate: how much of the sun a relief shadow cuts, 0 none to 1 all; the sky still lights it. Full only

sunCut._about: Seen from afar, rough ground returns less sun than a flat surface lit the same way, because its own bumps, blades and twigs shade one another. Where the scans' small shadows are too small to draw (beyond a few metres, and everywhere on Light), each kind of ground cuts this share of the direct sun instead. Estimates: the code-made ground before range-day-eight darkened grass and scrub by 5 to 12 percent through its drawn clumps, which is what brought the February slopes near their measured colours (switching that detail off on the old ground gives exactly the colour the photographed ground gives).

floor.estimate: packed dirt: clods and crumbs a few millimetres high, little self-shade

dry-grass.estimate: dry straw lying flat on the soil: little self-shade

green-grass.estimate: dense standing green grass: the blades shade the lower blades and the soil, about a fifth of the sun lost at the midday angles of the winter photographs

scrub-litter.estimate: ground classed as scrub is, from afar, dense brush over litter: about a fifth of the sun lost in its own shade

rock.estimate: eroded rock faces: flakes and cracks, little self-shade

scree.estimate: loose stones: each stone's shadow on its neighbours

air._about: The air between the eye and the ground (range-day-six): things pale toward the sky's colour with distance and brighten toward the sun; the distance comes from the day's humidity (haze.visibilityDryMi and visibilityHumidMi).

brightness.estimate: the brightness of the air's own light against a white surface in the sun (the far hills pale toward this), on a clear day

brightnessHumid.estimate: the same on the most humid day: a milky, bright haze

sunGlow.estimate: how much brighter the air is when looking toward the sun (forward scattering), as a share of its brightness

sunGlowWidth.estimate: how narrowly the glow sits around the sun's direction (the exponent of the cosine): 6 is a wide, soft glow

blueShare.estimate: how much of the air's colour is the sky's blue (the rest is the pale haze colour); the far hills go blue before they go pale

brush._about: What grows on the range (range-day-six): the kinds of plant the picture stands where the photograph is dark with scrub, their share of the count, their brightness within the measured scrub colour, the grass clumps, the tufts and stones on the floor, and the shadow under a bush. Every figure is an estimate with its basis.

sage.estimate: low rounded sage makes up about 45 percent of the bushes stood: the grey-green scrub that covers the left slope

chamise.estimate: taller, more open chamise-like shrubs about 30 percent

grass.estimate: dry grass clumps about 25 percent, on the grassy slopes and sparsely on the floor

sageBrightness.estimate: sage is a little paler than the measured scrub colour (grey-green leaves): 1.15 times it

chamiseBrightness.estimate: chamise is darker and more olive: 0.85 times the measured scrub colour

low.estimate: a grass clump stands about 0.8 ft

grassFarYd.estimate: grass clumps are stood out to 600 yards; beyond that they are smaller than a pixel through any sight and the ground's own grass texture carries them

floorTuftShare.estimate: about 12 percent of the grass clumps are sparse weeds on the floor between the line and the first boards (docs/LOOK.md: 'sparse weeds, green in winter and straw in summer')

floorReachYd.estimate: tufts and stones are stood on the floor inside 150 yards

stones.estimate: about five hundred stones on the floor inside that reach, on the Full picture (a third on Light)

low.estimate: a stone on the floor is 2 in across

high.estimate: to 10 in, the big ones rare

shadowDarkness.estimate: the ground right under a bush is darkened by 45 percent at the middle of its shadow, fading to nothing at the edge

picture._about: How the picture is drawn to the screen (range-day-six).

samplesFull.estimate: the Full picture smooths edges by drawing each pixel from four samples (multisampling); Light draws one

groundBytesFull.estimate: the most the photographed ground surfaces may add to the canyon course on Full: the range-day-eight brief's limit, on top of the 11,670,196 bytes the course weighed before

groundBytesLight.estimate: the same on Light, on top of 6,344,136 bytes
